steps: Losing late, a team sends its goaltender to the bench.
In his place comes an extra attacker: six skaters against five. Nothing is toggled on this site to show it — the goalie is simply no longer drawn.

steps: In each end — four spots, two on either side of the net. An icing comes back to one of these, in the offending team’s own end.
At centre ice — where a period starts, and where play restarts after every goal.
In the neutral zone — four more, just outside each blue line. A play called back out of the zone usually restarts here.

steps: A player shoots the puck from behind the centre line.
It crosses the far goal line with nobody touching it.
Play stops, and the face-off comes all the way back to the shooting team’s own end — that dot is the whole punishment.

steps: The puck carrier comes up the ice toward the blue line.
A teammate crosses the line before the puck does — that is offside. The puck has to cross the line completely first: touching it is not being in the zone.
Play stops, and the face-off comes back outside the zone.
